attempted_claim: Let p be a prime, k an algebraic extension of F_p, G a height-2 formal group law over k, and E=E(k,G) the associated Lubin–Tate E-infinity ring spectrum. Let x: MU<0> -> E be the unique H-infinity MU<0>-orientation corresponding to the norm-coherent coordinate (Zhu, Norm coherence, Theorem 1.2 / Corollary 8.17). Does x lift to a map of E-infinity ring spectra MU -> E; equivalently in Hopkins–Lawson terms, does the MX_1-orientation extend through MX_p to MX_{p^2} (which controls the K(2)-local E-infinity orientation tower, constant above p^2)? Decide existence and, if it exists, uniqueness, at least for the Honda law over F_p or a supersingular-elliptic height-2 case.
decisive_failure: originality: Senger Theorem 1.4 plus Corollary 1.5, combined with Zhu Theorem 1.2, substantively implies and strictly dominates the headline: Senger proves EVERY Ando-satisfying complex orientation of EVERY height<=2 even Landweber exact E-infinity ring lifts uniquely to MU->E, and deduces it for every E(k,G) with k algebraic over F_p via Zhu. The submitted norm-coherent H-infinity x is one such Ando orientation, so existence and uniqueness for all height-2 G including Honda and supersingular-elliptic cases is a mechanical corollary of the published stronger fact, not a new theorem.
